title: Paul of the Cross (1694–1775)
hook: he founds the Passionists to remember Christ's passion

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Paraguay missions, called reducción in Spanish: Guaraní towns, red stone, and carved angels with harps. Your line was the reductions. Did you learn a word of Guaraní? Today, a preacher who carried one thing everywhere he went. Day eight hundred eighty-five.

Sewn on the chest of a black habit is a badge shaped like a heart, with a small cross rising from its top. Inside the heart, in Latin, the words: the Passion of Jesus Christ. The men and women who wear it today are called Passionists. The badge goes back to an Italian man from a merchant family, who said he saw himself dressed this way in prayer, before any such habit existed. He went on to preach in Italian villages, carrying a crucifix. His name in religion was Paul of the Cross.
screen: `A BLACK HABIT.` → `A HEART WITH A CROSS.` → `THE PASSION OF JESUS CHRIST.`

segments.voice: First, the call. As a young man, Paolo Danei felt drawn to a life of prayer and penance. Tradition says that in prayer he saw the black habit and the sign of the Passion, and understood that he was to gather companions who would wear it. He went on retreat and wrote a rule for them. Second, the companions. It was slow. Few joined at first. His own brother, John Baptist, stayed beside him. They lived simply on a mountain on the coast of Tuscany, praying and fasting, and the community grew, eventually with nuns as well. Third, the preaching. Passionists went out to farm towns and villages to preach missions: days of sermons, confession and prayer. Paul preached holding a crucifix, telling people about the sufferings of Christ as a sign of how much God loved them. Passionists take a special vow to keep the memory of the Passion alive. Fourth, the darkness. His letters show that for long years his own prayer felt dry and empty, as if God were far away. He kept preaching the cross while carrying one inside. He died in Rome, and the Church canonized him. In the letter to the Galatians, in the Douay-Rheims, Saint Paul the apostle writes: "But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ." Paul of the Cross made that sentence his life's work.
screen: `A HABIT SEEN IN PRAYER.` · `SLOW YEARS, A BROTHER BESIDE HIM.` · `PREACHING WITH A CRUCIFIX.` · `HIS OWN LONG DARKNESS.` · then, large: `SAVE IN THE CROSS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: sit with a crucifix or a cross. If there's one in your home, hold it in your hand, or put a picture of one on your phone in front of you. Settle, and breathe. Don't study it. Just stay with it, the way Paul stayed through his dry years. Bring to mind one person who is suffering right now, and let the cross and that person rest together in your mind. Paul of the Cross believed love could be seen here. If you pray, you can simply stay there with Christ in silence, and bring that person with you. If you don't, let the image show you what someone gave for others, and stay with that. The bell holds the time.
Paolo Danei. The birth name of Paul of the Cross, who saw himself in prayer wearing a black habit with the sign of the Passion, before it existed.
Your line: remember the passion. Today, when you pass a cross, on a wall, a steeple or a necklace, pause for one breath and let it be more than decoration. Day eight hundred eighty-five.

screen: `DAY 885 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: ALWAYS IN NEED OF RENEWAL.`

howItsDone: Passionist priests, brothers and nuns wear the sign of the Passion on their habits and still preach parish missions and lead retreats centered on the cross, and Catholics often pray before a crucifix, especially on Fridays and in Lent.

original.note: Latin: the Passion of Jesus Christ, the words on the Passionist badge. XPI abbreviates Christi.

trapdoor: what you thought: a saint with a gloomy fixation on suffering.
what it means: a preacher who held up the crucifix as the clearest sign of how much God loves people.
what a scholar hears: a founder whose letters record long inner darkness, and a community bound by a vow to remember the Passion.

notes: Claims rule: the index's dates (1694–1775) appear only in the title; no counts stated (e.g., the forty-day retreat at Castellazzo, decades of dryness) in the spoken script.
The vision of the habit and sign attributed to tradition; confirm wording.
Monte Argentario (coast of Tuscany) as the early home of the community; brother John Baptist Danei; Passionist nuns: confirm.
'Passionists take a special vow' to promote the memory of the Passion (the fourth vow): confirm.
Badge text 'Jesu XPI Passio' and ecclesiastical pronunciation: confirm.
Practice says Paul believed the crucifix is 'where love could be seen most clearly'; confirm this (now: love could be seen here) is a fair paraphrase of his teaching.
